initial_observation_window_correction.diagnosis: Observer coverage equals the exact model tick count and all RAM/counters pass. Native result ticks measure the render interval and exclude control setup/completion; the initial ticks+10 assumption was wrong. Snapshot existing skip_stats calls to verify exact interval and zero bus traffic outside it.

findings: All observed AXI requests occupy one 64-byte-bus beat (4-byte or64-byte reads, 64-byte masked writes). Widening the bus alone leaves the number of beats per current request unchanged.

No observed AR/AW/W/R/B valid-and-not-ready cycles; the callback memory model returns every transaction in one cycle. These observations do not model physical DRAM latency or establish hardware bandwidth needs.
The sampler has no owner-capacity stalls and peaks at9/16 slots on full640. Requests are accepted on99.27% of cycles with any worker request, despite per-worker arbitration contention.
The current full640 vector-sample stage spends66.90% of worker-cycles fetching,14.31% blending and14.31% presenting results. Overlapping a successor with the blend is the next measured RTL target.
limitations: Observer elapsed overlaps other functional runs and is diagnostic only; no host-speed inference.

Native result ticks measure submit-to-completion; observer ticks also include control setup and completion reads. Exact existing skip_stats snapshots prove all measured bus traffic falls inside the task interval.
Sampler state residency aggregates worker-cycles and does not directly predict end-to-end elapsed savings.
The fixed full trace ends with two sampler word requests pending; accepted-minus-retired and occupancy are conserved.
